name: review-heavy-delivery-greenfield
description: Guided greenfield setup for changes requiring architecture, independent code review before test execution, test evidence, and final QA acceptance.

questions.prompt: How much delivery assurance does the change require?

options.label: Independent review and final QA
options.reason: Recommended because the workflow includes architecture, independent code review, test evidence, and QA acceptance.

options.label: Release-critical change
options.reason: Compatible because failed review, test, or QA gates cannot be bypassed and unresolved work returns for correction.

options.label: Minimal delivery process
options.reason: Blocked because this setup deliberately includes separate architecture, review, test, and QA phases. Use the lean-delivery setup for focused lower-risk changes.

questions.prompt: When should independent code review occur?

options.label: Before test execution
options.reason: Recommended because maintainability, correctness, test design, and security findings are corrected before the formal test and QA phases.

options.label: Before final QA acceptance
options.reason: Blocked because this setup deliberately performs independent code review before formal test execution. Use the orchestrated-delivery setup when review should occur after tests and immediately before final QA.

options.label: Implementation self-review only
options.reason: Blocked because the Implementer must not self-approve implementation work.

options.label: Review after release
options.reason: Blocked because review is a fail-closed gate and must complete before test execution and QA acceptance.

questions.prompt: Which target agent platforms should be generated?

options.label: OpenCode and VS Code Copilot
options.reason: Recommended because both registered target adapters are generated from the same validated composition.

options.label: OpenCode only
options.reason: Compatible because the OpenCode adapter is registered.

options.label: VS Code Copilot only
options.reason: Compatible because the VS Code Copilot adapter is registered.
